summary: LayerBudget proposes a per-layer joint allocation of token budget n_l and KV bit-width b_l via a greedy marginal-gain solver, with a Gini-based coverage law, a sigmoid 'inverted importance' prior, and mean-fill for evicted positions. On a 15-minute skim the paper does not survive. (1) The abstract's headline number is falsified by the paper's own table: 'PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' is contradicted by Table 19, where Llama-2-13B is 1.11 at 4x; the parenthetical silently carves it out with 'at GQA'. (2) The main results table (Table 2, p6) renders visibly broken -- the Qwen3-8B column group is stranded across a large gap with its 6x column detached from its 2x/3x/4x cells, and \resizebox has shrunk the body to roughly 4pt, below legibility and a NeurIPS font-size risk. (3) Figure 1 (right) directly contradicts its own caption: the caption says LayerBudget 'outperforms all eviction methods', but the plotted red curve at CR=6x sits at 1.25, above H2O (1.158) and SnapKV (1.245); the StreamLLM curve is silently clipped by the y-limit at 1.35. (4) Figures 2 and 3 -- the only figures illustrating the method's mechanism -- are drawn on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears nowhere in the seven-model evaluation suite, at unreadable print size, with an orphan FP16 legend entry that is never used in any panel, red/green encoding that is colorblind-unsafe, and two panels of Figure 3 that use different colors for the same two series. (5) Against the strongest baseline the method ties or loses: KIVI beats or matches LayerBudget on PPL at 3x/4x/6x on every model in Table 2, matches it on MMLU (Table 11), GSM8K (Table 15) and LongBench (Table 17), and ties on NIAH on 3 of 4 models (Table 12); the entire differentiator is 2 needle failures on one model. Table 10 shows quant-only dominating the joint method at 6x (1.00 vs 3.23 on Mistral; 1.01 vs 45.09 on Llama-2), and the rebuttal is a caption paragraph, not a measurement. (6) Table 13 reports 24.3% measured memory saving at nominal CR=2x on Llama-2-7B, i.e. an effective 1.32x, while Appendix E asserts every method's effective CR matches nominal 'within +/-0.05'. That is a hard, checkable self-contradiction in the paper's central axis. A hurried reader comes away unable to state a defended claim, and with the impression that the figures and the main table were not looked at after compilation.
strengths: The core question is real and well-motivated in one sentence: eviction and quantization have different cost structures, so a per-layer joint (n_l, b_l) allocation should beat applying either uniformly. The 'quantize first, evict last' slogan in the abstract is the one part of the pitch that lands immediately on a skim.

The empirical footprint is unusually broad for this problem: seven models from 7B to 72B spanning MHA and GQA, 17 reimplemented baselines behind one interface, 16K/32K long-context PPL, and five task families (WikiText-2, MMLU, GSM8K, LongBench, NIAH/RULER). Very few submissions in this area evaluate at 72B at all.

The paper is unusually candid where it could have hidden things: Section 3.5 explicitly declines the (1-1/e) submodular bound and says why the action graph is not a matroid; Section 7(5) states outright that shared-b_l is dominated at 6x by MoE-nD; Table 2's footnote flags MiniKV's 11.92 as a measured value rather than deleting the cell; Appendix E documents a memory-denominator inconsistency in Table 7 rather than quietly regenerating it.

The mean-fill result is the paper's one genuinely striking and cleanly isolated number: on Llama-2-7B at 6x, PPL ratio moves from 45.09 (zero-fill, Table 3) to 1.13 (mean-fill, Section 6), with logits KL dropping 0.6696 -> 0.0636. That is a large, reproducible effect from a one-line change and is useful to the field independent of the rest of the method.

The MoE-nD and xKV head-to-heads (Table 1, Table 6) are presented with the losing cells visible and bolded for the competitor (MoE-nD 1.038 bolded at Mistral 6x), which is more honest than most concurrent-work comparisons.
weaknesses: FALSIFIED HEADLINE NUMBER (abstract, l.12-13 vs Table 19, p19). The abstract claims 'PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B'. Table 19 reports Llama-2-13B at 4x = 1.11, which is one of the seven models and violates the stated bound by 8pp. The parenthetical '(1.00-1.03 on the 7B suite, <=1.01 on 13B-72B at GQA)' hides the miss by restricting the 13B-72B claim to GQA -- the only MHA model above 7B is exactly the one that fails. FIX: state the bound over the models it actually holds for, or report the 13B MHA number in the headline sentence.

BROKEN MAIN RESULTS TABLE AS RENDERED (Table 2, p6). In the compiled PDF the fourth column group is structurally broken: the 'Qwen3-8B (GQA)' header and its cmidrule span an empty region, the sub-headers read '2x 3x 4x' immediately after the Llama-3.1 group and then a lone '6x' far to the right, and every data row shows three Qwen3 values butted against the Llama-3.1 block with the 6x value stranded at the page edge (H2O: '... 1.08 1.12 1.18 [gap] 1.24'). The cause is the \multicolumn{18} footnote inside the tabular, whose natural width is dumped into the last column. Compounding this, \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} shrinks the body text to roughly 4pt -- the footnote line is not readable at print size at all. This is the single table a reviewer looks at first, and it is both unreadable and visibly wrong. FIX: move the footnote outside the tabular (\begin{tablenotes} or a caption addendum), drop \resizebox, and split into two tables if 18 columns do not fit at \small.

FIGURE 1 CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CAPTION AND CLIPS A CURVE (p7). The caption reads 'LayerBudget (bold) outperforms all eviction methods and matches KIVI at 2-3x.' In the right panel the red LayerBudget curve rises to ~1.25 at CR=6x, crossing above both H2O (green, ~1.158) and SnapKV (grey, ~1.245). The figure as drawn shows the method losing to two eviction baselines. Separately, the StreamLLM curve runs into the top frame at y=1.35 and its 4x and 6x points simply vanish with no break marker or note. FIX: either extend the y-axis (log scale) so no series is truncated, or restrict the panel to 2-4x and say so; and rewrite the caption to 'outperforms all eviction methods at 2-4x'.

MECHANISM FIGURES ARE ON A MODEL THAT IS NEVER EVALUATED, AND ARE ILLEGIBLE (Figures 2 and 3, p7). Both figures are drawn on TinyLlama-1.1B (22 layers), which appears nowhere in the seven-model suite (Setup, p5) and in no results table. Figure 2's legend advertises three precision levels (FP16 green / INT8 orange / INT4 red) but FP16 never appears in any of the four panels -- an orphan legend entry that also contradicts Section 1's claim that the allocator 'upgrades from INT4 to INT8/FP16 only at sensitive layers'. The 4x panel is uniformly INT4, i.e. no per-layer precision at the headline compression ratio. Axis tick labels, panel titles and the right-hand 'Gini' axis are all sub-3pt and unreadable at print size. Figure 3 uses blue/green for (Gini, importance) in the left panel and orange/red for the same two series in the right panel; the rho annotation box overlaps the frame and is unreadable; the pink and blue shaded bands are labelled only in an illegible legend and are never defined in the caption or text. Green-vs-red (Fig 2) and orange-vs-red (Fig 3) are the two worst pairs for deuteranopia and they carry the only encoding channel. FIX: redraw both on Mistral-7B or Llama-3.1-8B, delete unused legend entries, set fonts >=7pt at final size, use one palette across panels, and define the shaded bands in the caption.

TIES OR LOSES TO THE STRONGEST BASELINE ON THE METRIC THAT MATTERS. KIVI is the fairest strong baseline and it wins or ties on PPL essentially everywhere at CR>=3x (Table 2 Mistral: KIVI 1.01/1.01/1.01 vs LB 1.01/1.03/1.25 at 3/4/6x; Table 19 Llama-2-13B: KIVI 1.02 flat vs LB 1.11/1.56 at 4/6x). It ties on MMLU (Table 11: 63.7 vs 64.1 on Llama-3.1, 76.6 vs 76.1 on Qwen2.5-14B -- KIVI higher), on GSM8K (Table 15: KIVI 9.0/22.0 vs LB 7.5/22.5 on Llama-2/Llama-3.1), on LongBench (Table 17: within 0.003 on all three models), and on NIAH for 3 of 4 models (Table 12: 100/100, 73.3/73.3, 100/100). The sole differentiating cell is Llama-2-7B NIAH, 93.3% vs 100% -- with 10 depths x 3 needles that is 28/30 vs 30/30, i.e. two needle failures, reported with no confidence interval. Worse, the paper's own Table 10 shows quant-only beating the joint method at 6x by 3.2x (Mistral) and 45x (Llama-2), and the response is a caption paragraph ('Under a memory-matched comparison ... quant-only ... degrades comparably') with no number attached. FIX: run the memory-matched quant-only-beyond-INT4 experiment the caption promises and report it, and repeat NIAH with enough needles to attach a CI to the 93.3 vs 100 gap.

THE COMPRESSION-RATIO AXIS IS NOT A CONTROLLED QUANTITY, AND THE PAPER'S OWN AUDIT CLAIM IS FALSE. Appendix E (p13) states 'every method's effective CR (= Full_KV_bytes / method_bytes) matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05 at the points reported in Table 2.' Table 13 (p16), at nominal CR=2x, reports Llama-2-7B 287 MB -> 218 MB (effective 1.32x), Mistral-7B 95 MB -> 54 MB (effective 1.76x), Llama-3.1-8B 189 MB -> 54 MB (effective 3.50x). All three violate the +/-0.05 claim, by up to 0.68, and the spread across models at one nominal CR is 1.32x-3.50x. This invalidates the cross-model comparison in Section 4.1 ('GQA models are more robust ... at matched compression') -- they were not at matched compression -- and it means the Llama-2-7B row of Table 2 compares LayerBudget at an effective 1.32x against eviction baselines nominally at 2x. FIX: report measured mean_memory_bytes per cell in Table 2 (or a per-cell effective-CR column), and rerun any comparison where the effective CRs differ by more than a few percent.

THE ALLOCATOR LATENCY CLAIM IS OFF BY THREE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE AND CONTRADICTS THREE OTHER PLACES IN THE PAPER. Section 3.4 (p4) says the allocator inner loop 'takes <1 ms in isolation on Mistral-7B at S=1024', and extrapolates Qwen2.5-72B at S=32K to '~10 ms ... still small relative to a single decode step'. Table 16 (p18) has a separate 'Gini' column (5.7-12 ms) and an 'Alloc' column (103-513 ms), and the Total column is arithmetically (AttnOH + Gini + Alloc)/Prefill -- verified on all six rows -- which proves Alloc EXCLUDES Gini. So the caption's reconciliation ('the bulk of Alloc is dominated by attention-row collection') and Section 3.4's ('the 100-513 ms in Table 16 is the full profiling pipeline ... not the allocator alone') are both arithmetically false, and Section 6 (p9) states the opposite outright: 'greedy allocator dominates at 100-513 ms, linear in S'. Taking the measured 301 ms at L=32, S=1024 (4096 iterations) gives 73.5 us/iteration, not 30 ns; the 72B/32K extrapolation (327,680 iterations) becomes ~24 s, not 10 ms. FIX: profile the allocator in isolation and report the real number, then restate the deployment story honestly (fixed profiles are the only viable path, and the paper should lead with that).

CHECKLIST CONTRADICTS THE BODY IN FOUR PLACES AND IS STALE (pp13-18). Item 3 justifies 'Theory assumptions and proofs: Yes' by citing 'the (1-1/e) approximation guarantee with a citation to Svirdenko 2004' -- Section 3.5 explicitly says 'We do not claim the standard (1-1/e) submodular bound' and cites Sviridenko only to explain why the bound does NOT apply. Item 1 says 'The abstract and Section 1 state five specific contributions'; the introduction lists six. Item 2 says Section 7 discusses 'four specific limitations ... and context length coverage (<=3500 tokens evaluated)'; Section 7 lists five, and the paper evaluates at 32K. Items 4 and 13 say 'All 12 baselines are named' and 'The 12 reimplemented baselines'; the paper claims 17 throughout. Item 7 answers 'No' to statistical significance on the grounds that 'run-to-run variance is zero', while Section 4.1 reports a paired-bootstrap 95% CI. A reviewer who reads the checklist -- and many do, first -- concludes the submission was assembled from stale drafts. FIX: regenerate the checklist against the current text; the (1-1/e) claim in particular must be removed.

OPERATING ENVELOPE IS AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE BELOW THE 2026 BAR, AND THE CLOSEST PRIOR WORK IS ABSENT. The paper's usable range is 2-4x (it degrades to 1.25 on Mistral, 1.56 on Llama-2-13B, and 45.09 zero-fill on Llama-2-7B at 6x). Concurrent and published work in this exact niche operates at 14x (MoE-nD), 20x (STAR-KV, ICML 2026 Spotlight), 20-40x (KVTC, ICLR 2026), and 2.48% retention (RDKV). RDKV -- which frames eviction and quantization as endpoints of one bit-allocation problem, i.e. this paper's thesis -- is not cited or compared. HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, public code) and PolyKV are likewise absent. NVIDIA KVPress, the de-facto harness with built-in PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache, is never mentioned despite the paper reimplementing 17 baselines by hand. FIX: cite and compare against RDKV and HqeKV at minimum, and report results through KVPress or justify the custom harness.

SEVERAL EVALUATIONS ARE AT THE FLOOR, MAKING 'MATCHES FULL KV' VACUOUS. Table 17 reports LongBench overall scores of 0.040-0.056 for every method including Full KV; published LongBench averages for these models are in the 25-45 range on a 0-100 scale, so these numbers are at or near zero and cannot distinguish any method -- yet the caption claims 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on all models'. Table 15 reports GSM8K Full KV = 5.5% on Llama-2-7B (11/200 correct), a floor at which 'preserves Full KV accuracy' carries no information, and LayerBudget 'beats' Full KV on 3 of 4 models with the difference waved off in a footnote as 'chain-of-thought variance at small n' rather than reported with a binomial CI. FIX: fix or drop the LongBench harness (the scale is clearly wrong), and either use a model that clears the GSM8K floor or drop the benchmark.

THE ABSTRACT IS A 21-LINE WALL OF NUMBERS WITH NO THESIS SENTENCE, AND ITS FIRST SENTENCE IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PAPER'S OWN TABLE 4. 'KV cache compression methods either evict tokens or quantize, but apply their strategy uniformly across layers' is stated without hedge; Table 4 (p12) marks PyramidKV, D2O, CAKE, Ada-KV, MiniKV, EVICPRESS and MoE-nD as per-layer or finer, and Related Work describes six such methods. The abstract then packs seven distinct result claims across four model scales, three metrics and five compression ratios into one block with no paragraph break, so the reader finishes it without a single retained claim. FIX: open with the gap in one sentence, state one headline result, and move the rest to the results section.

APPENDIX B IS AN EMPTY SECTION IN THE COMPILED PDF (p12). The heading 'B Positioning vs Prior Work' is followed immediately by 'C LayerBudget-KV mechanism and asymmetry' with zero body text; the section's only content, Table 4, floats above the heading. Small, but it is the kind of thing a skimming reviewer registers as 'not proofread after compilation', alongside the broken Table 2 and the checklist staleness.

RELATED WORK CONTAINS WHAT READS AS REBUTTAL TEXT ADDRESSED TO REVIEWERS (p3). A 32-line unbroken paragraph carries an embedded 'Caveat on baselines:' passage that pre-attributes any disagreement with MoE-nD's and xKV's published numbers to '(a) different evaluation harness ... (b) calibration differences, or (c) implementation gaps -- we will update against their official code at camera-ready', and concludes the head-to-head loss at 6x with 'The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers.' Appendix E likewise promises 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table 7'. Deferred fixes and pre-emptive excuses in the submitted body read as a paper arguing with a prior review rather than making a case. FIX: move the caveat to a short footnote, and regenerate Table 7 before submitting rather than promising to.
questions: Table 13 reports 24.3% measured KV savings at nominal CR=2x on Llama-2-7B (effective 1.32x), 42.9% on Mistral-7B (1.76x), and 71.2% on Llama-3.1-8B (3.50x), while Appendix E asserts effective CR matches nominal within +/-0.05 at every point in Table 2. Which of these two statements is correct? If Table 13 is correct, what are the per-cell effective CRs for every LayerBudget entry in Table 2, and do any comparisons reverse once the baselines are matched to the same measured byte budget?

Table 16 lists 'Gini' (5.7-12 ms) and 'Alloc' (103-513 ms) as separate columns, and the Total column equals (AttnOH + Gini + Alloc)/Prefill on all six rows, so Alloc excludes Gini extraction. How is that reconciled with Section 3.4's '<1 ms in isolation' and the ~10 ms extrapolation to Qwen2.5-72B at 32K? Please report a standalone profile of the allocator inner loop, and the measured (not extrapolated) allocation time on Qwen2.5-72B at S=32K.

Contribution 1 (the greedy marginal-gain solver) is isolated only against 500-trial random search on the surrogate quality score Q, giving 118-119%. Is there an experiment isolating the solver's effect on PPL or any downstream metric relative to (a) random search and (b) a fixed pyramid schedule? As it stands, Table 3 shows the hand-set sigmoid direction is worth up to 45x in PPL ratio and Table 10's A3 shows the INT8 level is worth 0.00-0.01, which inverts the credit ordering the abstract implies.

Table 10's A3 row shows {4,16} and {4,8,16} give bit-identical PPL ratios (3.23/3.23 on Mistral, 45.09/45.09 on Llama-2 at 6x; 1.02/1.02 at 3x). If the INT8 level never changes the outcome, on what evidence is per-layer mixed precision -- the 'Precision' half of the title -- a contribution rather than an unused degree of freedom? Which table shows a setting where the allocator's chosen bit-widths are non-uniform AND that non-uniformity measurably helps?

Figures 2 and 3 are drawn on TinyLlama-1.1B, which is absent from the seven-model suite. Do the allocation patterns and the rho=0.194 Gini/importance decorrelation hold on the models you actually evaluate? Note that rho=0.194 over 22 layers is not significantly different from zero (p ~ 0.4), so 'weak correlation confirms complementary signals' is not supported by that measurement.

How is the mixed-bit {4,8,16} cache physically laid out at inference time? Is there a packed kernel, or is each layer dequantized to FP16 before attention? Table 13's Speedup column is below 1x in all nine rows (0.88x-0.99x) and Table 14 shows +2.6% to +12.2% TPOT overhead, which suggests the mixed-precision cache is not realized in a fused kernel -- if so, the M(n,b) = 2nHd*b/8 memory model in Eq. 1 overstates the achievable saving.

Why are RDKV (rate-distortion joint eviction+quantization), HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, code public) and PolyKV not cited or compared, and why is the evaluation not run through NVIDIA KVPress, which provides PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache behind the same API you reimplemented 17 baselines to obtain?

Table 17's LongBench scores are 0.040-0.056 for every method including Full KV. What scale are these on, and what is Full KV's published LongBench score for Mistral-7B under your harness? If the harness is producing near-floor scores, the 'matches Full KV on LongBench' claim in Section 6 and the conclusion should be withdrawn.

probe_answers.answer: Alternatives that plausibly solve the same problem: (1) RDKV (rate-distortion bit allocation for JOINT eviction and quantization; explicitly argues the two actions 'must be explored jointly rather than in a staged fashion', reverse water-filling + discrete knapsack over hardware bit-widths, TriZone packed-decode kernel, 97.81% of full-cache LongBench accuracy at 2.48% retention) -- IGNORED ENTIRELY; not cited anywhere in the 80-entry bibliography (pp10-11). This is the single closest alternative and it subsumes the paper's thesis with a principled objective in place of the paper's hand-set sigmoid. (2) HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, hybrid quantization+eviction with an integrated per-element optimizer and a joint K-V importance metric, public code) -- IGNORED ENTIRELY. Public code removes the paper's stated excuse for reimplementing MoE-nD/xKV. (3) PolyKV (layer-wise design space coupling eviction pattern and capacity under a shared budget) -- IGNORED ENTIRELY. (4) STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight; low-rank + mixed-precision quantization, 20x, custom kernels) -- IGNORED. (5) KVTC (ICLR 2026, NVIDIA; PCA + adaptive quantization + entropy coding under a global bit budget, 20-40x) -- IGNORED. (6) Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026; layer-wise budget allocation, RULER at 20% cache: 91.4 vs SnapKV 39.0) -- IGNORED. (7) NVIDIA KVPress, the de-facto harness with built-in PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache -- IGNORED; the paper hand-reimplements 17 baselines without mentioning it, which matters because the query-visibility audit shows a backend swap (sdpa->eager) moves RULER by -0.221, larger than most method gaps. Compared head-to-head: only MoE-nD (Table 1) and xKV (Table 6), both as the authors' own re-implementations, and the classic 2024-25 eviction/quantization set. Argued-insufficient: none of the ignored systems. Verdict: at least six obvious alternatives ignored, one of them (RDKV) being the same idea with a better-founded objective and results an order of magnitude beyond this paper's envelope. Fatal weakness.

(1) 'PPL ratio' -- the paper's central metric, used seven times in the abstract before any definition; first defined on p5 ('measuring PPL ratio (compressed/full)'). A reader who stops after the abstract does not know whether lower or higher is better or what the denominator is. (2) 'GQA' / 'MHA' -- used in the abstract ('<=1.01 on 13B-72B at GQA') and never expanded anywhere in the paper; grouped-query attention and multi-head attention are never spelled out once. (3) 'CR' -- used in Figure 1's axis, Figure 2's caption and the intro; defined only in Section 4 (p5). (4) 'mean-fill' -- used in the abstract before definition; the abstract is the standalone artifact and it is not self-contained. (5) 'closed-form coverage law' (Related Work, p3, l.92) -- forward-references Eq. 3, which appears on p4. (6) SYMBOL OVERLOAD: b is 'the per-element byte-width' in Section 1 (p1, l.25) but 'the quantization bit-width' b_l in {4,8,16} in Section 3.1 (p3, l.126); M(n,b)=2nHd*b/8 divides by 8, confirming b is bits there. Same symbol, two units, three pages apart. (7) LAYER INDEX OVERLOAD: Eq. 1 sums l=1..L and Eq. 4 uses l/(L-1), but every empirical statement is 0-based ('restoring layers 0-10', 'layers 26-39 vs 0-12'). Eq. 4 is only well-formed for 0-based l; the formulation is 1-based. (8) 'Cat.' row labels in Table 2 -- 'Evict', 'Ph', 'Qt', 'Jt' are never expanded in the caption or the text. 'Ph' and 'Jt' are unguessable on a skim. (9) 'LB' -- used as the method name in Tables 12 and 20 and in Section 4.1 ('LB degrades 3-25%') without ever being introduced as an abbreviation. (10) 'Protected band' / 'Compress-first band' -- the shaded regions in Figure 3 are labelled only inside an illegible legend and are defined nowhere in caption or text. (11) 'quality' / Q -- Q(l,n_l,b_l) is called 'a quality model' but what quantity it approximates (PPL? attention mass? logit fidelity?) is never stated; the calibration checks only the coverage factor C against attention mass (MAE 3.1%), never Q against any quality metric. (12) 'quality score' in contribution 1 ('118-119% of the best 500-trial random-search quality score') -- an undefined objective value, not a reported metric, presented in the contributions list as if it were a result. Twelve items found; more than the required five.

RECOMPUTE A (Table 16, p18 -- the least-checked derivation). Claim under test: Section 3.4 (p4) 'the allocator's inner loop ... takes <1 ms in isolation on Mistral-7B at S=1024' and 'The figure of 100-513 ms in Table 16 is the full profiling pipeline (Gini extraction across all layers, plus the allocator), not the allocator alone.' Table 16 has separate Gini and Alloc columns. Test whether Total = (AttnOH + Gini + Alloc)/Prefill, which would prove Alloc excludes Gini. Llama S=256: AttnOH = +9.7% x 163 = +15.8 ms; (15.8 + 5.7 + 103)/163 = 124.5/163 = 76.4% -> table says +77%. Llama S=512: -2.2% x 241 = -5.3; (-5.3 + 17 + 160)/241 = 171.7/241 = 71.2% -> table says +71%. Llama S=1024: -0.6% x 447 = -2.7; (-2.7 + 12 + 301)/447 = 310.3/447 = 69.4% -> table says +70%. Mistral S=256: +8.6% x 167 = +14.4; (14.4 + 7.6 + 120)/167 = 142/167 = 85.0% -> +85%. Mistral S=512: -5.4% x 261 = -14.1; (-14.1 + 7.0 + 167)/261 = 159.9/261 = 61.3% -> +61%. Mistral S=1024: -0.6% x 476 = -2.9; (-2.9 + 9.3 + 513)/476 = 519.4/476 = 109.1% -> +109%. All six rows check out to within rounding, which PROVES Alloc is a line item disjoint from Gini. Therefore Section 3.4's reconciliation and Table 16's own caption ('the bulk of Alloc is dominated by attention-row collection') are arithmetically false, and Section 6 (p9, l.336) states the truth: 'greedy allocator dominates at 100-513 ms'. RECOMPUTE B (the extrapolation, p4). Stated model: O(L * S/dn) iterations, dn=8, '~30 ns per iteration'. At L=32, S=1024: 32 * 128 = 4096 iterations. Measured Alloc = 301 ms (Llama) / 513 ms (Mistral) -> 73.5 us and 125 us per iteration, i.e. 2450x-4170x the asserted 30 ns. Applying the measured 73.5 us/iteration to the paper's own Qwen2.5-72B case (80 * 32768/8 = 327,680 iterations) gives 24.1 seconds, not the claimed '~10 ms ... still small relative to a single decode step'. The extrapolation is wrong by ~2400x and reverses its own conclusion. RECOMPUTE C (Appendix E's audit claim vs Table 13). Appendix E: effective CR matches nominal 'within +/-0.05 at the points reported in Table 2'. Table 13 at nominal CR=2x: Llama-2-7B 287/218 = 1.317x (error 0.68); Mistral-7B 95/54 = 1.759x (error 0.24); Llama-3.1-8B 189/54 = 3.500x (error 1.50). All three fail the stated bound, two of them by more than an order of magnitude beyond it. All three recomputations expose defects.

The most favorable-sounding abstract number is not the honest one, in three ways. (a) SCOPE. 'PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' is false: Table 19 gives Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x. The parenthetical restricts the 13B-72B claim 'at GQA', silently excluding the only non-GQA model in that range -- the one that misses. (b) BUDGET. The headline comparisons in Table 2 are at nominal CR, but Table 13 shows the measured byte reduction at nominal CR=2x is 1.32x on Llama-2-7B, 1.76x on Mistral and 3.50x on Llama-3.1. On the MHA model the method is therefore compared at an effective 1.32x against eviction baselines nominally given 2x -- the most favorable direction. The paper flags this risk in the 'CR definition' paragraph and says it 'flags every cell where method-byte CR diverges', but Table 2 contains no such flags and the only reconciliation (Appendix E) covers a single 6x Mistral point. (c) BASELINE CONFIGURATION. H2O's collapse numbers do most of the rhetorical work (83.4x at 32K/4x; 42.2% MMLU vs Full KV 63.9%). The paper defends this in Table 11's caption -- a faithful per-head H2O gives 29.4%, even worse -- but H2O at 4x FP16 is being asked to hold a token budget where any FP16 eviction method fails, while LayerBudget spends most of its budget on INT4 quantization. That is a comparison between compression axes, not between allocation policies. The honest framing would be against KIVI at matched bytes, and there LayerBudget ties or loses (see P14). Separately, GSM8K on Llama-2-7B is run at a floor (Full KV = 5.5%, 11/200), so 'preserves Full KV accuracy' there is unfalsifiable, and LayerBudget's 7.5% 'beating' Full KV is explained away in a footnote rather than with a CI. Defect confirmed.

Ten internal contradictions, all checkable on the rendered pages. (1) Abstract 'PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models' vs Table 19 Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x. (2) Table 2 caption 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods at every setting' vs Table 2's own Mistral 6x column: H2O 1.16 and SnapKV 1.24 both beat LayerBudget's 1.25. The Section 4.1 bullet self-refutes in one sentence: 'ranks first at every CR on every model. At 6x ... LB degrades 3-25% while H2O degrades 11-24%' -- 25 > 24. (3) Figure 1 caption 'outperforms all eviction methods' vs the plotted crossover at CR=6x. (4) Section 3.4 '<1 ms' allocator vs Section 6 'greedy allocator dominates at 100-513 ms' vs Table 16's caption, which asserts a third, arithmetically impossible reading (see P3). (5) Appendix E 'effective CR matches nominal within +/-0.05' vs Table 13's 1.32x/1.76x/3.50x at nominal 2x. (6) Checklist item 3 credits the paper with 'the (1-1/e) approximation guarantee with a citation to Svirdenko 2004' vs Section 3.5 'We do not claim the standard (1-1/e) submodular bound ... the action graph is not a matroid in the form required by [Sviridenko]'. (7) Checklist item 1 'five specific contributions' vs six numbered contributions in Section 1; item 2 'four specific limitations ... (<=3500 tokens evaluated)' vs five limitations and 32K evaluation; items 4 and 13 'All 12 baselines' vs 17 throughout the body. (8) Checklist item 7 answers 'No' to statistical significance ('run-to-run variance is zero') vs Section 4.1's 'paired-bootstrap 95% CI ... [-0.003, +0.002]'. (9) Section 7(4) 'Downstream tasks (MMLU, GSM8K) at 72B were prohibitively slow ... we report PPL, NIAH, and RULER' vs Table 21's footnote reporting 'MMLU Full KV=81.2%' at 72B. (10) Section 1 and 3.4 claim the allocator 'upgrades from INT4 to INT8/FP16 only at sensitive layers' vs Figure 2, in which FP16 appears in the legend and in zero panels, and Table 10's A3 row, in which removing INT8 entirely ({4,16} vs {4,8,16}) changes nothing. Bonus: 'Mistral-7B at 6x' appears as 1.250 (Table 1), 1.25 (Table 2), 1.07 (Table 7), 1.283 (Table 3) and 3.23 (Tables 8/10) under different seq lengths and fill modes, none of which is signposted at the point of use.

The prose does not read as freshly machine-generated, but it does read as accreted-under-review, which produces a similar surface: sections that describe rather than argue, and defensive framing where a result should be. Specific sentences. (a) The 32-line unbroken Related Work paragraph on p3 is the clearest tell -- it opens as positioning, pivots mid-paragraph into a head-to-head results report ('A head-to-head experiment on two 7B models (Table 1) shows...'), then into a defensive block ('Caveat on baselines: the MoE-nD and xKV rows ... are our faithful re-implementations ... any divergence from the original authors' reported numbers should be attributed to (a) different evaluation harness ... (b) calibration differences, or (c) implementation gaps -- we will update against their official code at camera-ready'), then back into positioning. That is a rebuttal thread pasted into the body, not an argued section. (b) Loss-as-feature reframing: 'The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers' -- a classic not-X-but-Y construction deployed exactly where the paper lost the comparison. (c) Assertion-as-explanation: 'This is intrinsic to the byte budget' (Table 10 caption) is offered in place of the memory-matched measurement the same caption then promises. (d) Defensive micro-annotations that a confident paper would not need: 'the value is the measured ratio (not a typo)' (Table 2 footnote); 'LB slightly exceeds Full KV due to chain-of-thought variance at small n' (Table 15 footnote); 'H2O on Llama-2-7B anomalously high due to degenerate repetition inflating F1' (Table 17 footnote); 'Speedup <1x due to compression overhead; amortized at higher batch sizes / longer generation' (Table 13 footnote, asserting an amortization that is never measured). (e) Deferred-fix language inside the submission: 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table 7 using mean_memory_bytes as the denominator' (Appendix E). Unexplained jargon density is moderate but real: 'closed-form coverage law', 'inverted importance', 'quantize-first regime', 'the eviction-dominated regime where the quality cliff is set by the model's tolerance for token loss' -- coined terms used as if established. The cumulative effect on a skim is that the paper is negotiating rather than reporting.

(a) OVER-ASSERTION. Abstract sentence 1: 'KV cache compression methods either evict tokens or quantize, but apply their strategy uniformly across layers' -- unhedged universal, contradicted by the paper's own Table 4, which marks PyramidKV/D2O/CAKE as per-layer evict, Ada-KV as per-head, KVTuner/XQuant as per-layer quant, and MoE-nD as all four. The intro softens to 'Nearly all' (p2, l.34) but the abstract does not. Table 2 caption: 'ranks 1st among all token-compression methods at every setting' -- false at Mistral 6x. Section 4.1: 'Among eviction and joint methods, LayerBudget ranks first at every CR on every model' -- same. Section 3.3: 'This weak correlation MEANS the two signals provide complementary information' -- rho=0.194 over 22 layers has p ~ 0.4; the honest verb is 'is consistent with', and the honest reading is 'we could not detect a correlation'. Section 4.2: 'attention sparsity profiles calibrated at short context transfer to 32K tokens without recalibration' -- stated as validated, but the supporting Gini-stability measurement (p9) covers 256-2048 tokens only. Section 6: 'confirming that quantization preserves global understanding' -- one MMLU table does not confirm that. (b) VAGUE REFERENT. 'These results validate the Gini stability finding from Section 6' (p7, l.255) -- 'These results' are long-context PPL ratios, which measure neither Gini nor stability; the antecedent does not support the predicate. 'This explains the NIAH advantage' (p9, l.325) -- 'This' points at a two-clause compound sentence with two candidate mechanisms. 'it autonomously avoids eviction' (p8, l.295) -- 'it' is 'the joint approach', 'the allocator', or 'the marginal-gain ranking', all three live in the preceding sentence. 'The reduction generalizes' (p8, l.302) -- 'the reduction' is the 96% KL reduction, but the sentence then reports a PPL reduction too. 'The two design points are therefore best read as...' (p3) -- which two, of the three variants (LayerBudget, LayerBudget-KV, MoE-nD) discussed in the preceding four sentences? (c) THING-VS-PROCESS CONFLATION. 'allocation' denotes both the artifact ('the allocation differs at every CR', 'per-layer plan dumps', p12) and the activity ('~327K iterations per allocation', '<1 ms in isolation', p4). 'profiling' denotes both the artifact ('fixed profiles (calibrated once per model)') and the activity ('profiling overhead adds 61-109%'), and the two are load-bearing in opposite directions in the same sentence (p9, l.335-337). 'compression' denotes the ratio ('at 4x compression'), the operation ('quantization achieves ~4x compression'), and the method class ('token-compression methods'). (d) FALSE PRECISION. 'reducing output distortion by 96%' (abstract, unqualified) is the single best of three measured models -- Llama-2-7B is 90.5%, Llama-3.1-8B 95.7%; the contributions list widens this to '96% and PPL degradation by 63-97%' without saying which model gives which. 'achieving 118-119% of the best 500-trial random-search quality score' quotes a 1pp-wide band to three significant figures from a stochastic baseline with no seeds, no repeats and no CI. 'Pearson rho = 0.194' is three decimals from n=22. 'inverted importance weights improve 6x compression by 60-94%' is computed as (r_base - r_new)/r_base on a PPL RATIO whose floor is 1.0 -- on Llama-2-7B that is (45.09-2.52)/45.09 = 94.4%, but the same improvement expressed over the excess-above-lossless is (45.09-2.52)/(45.09-1) = 96.5%, and neither number is a meaningful percentage of anything a reader cares about. 'MAE 3.1%' for the coverage law is reported for one model with no spread.

THESIS (one sentence, reconstructed without headings): 'Because transformer layers differ in attention sparsity, a training-free online solver that jointly chooses a token budget and a KV bit-width per layer beats applying eviction or quantization uniformly, at 2-4x compression.' TOPIC SENTENCES AND MAPPING. p1: 'The KV cache is the primary memory bottleneck' -> maps. 'Two families have emerged' -> maps. p2: 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' -> maps to thesis but its evidence (Gini 0.43-0.93 on TinyLlama-1.1B) is from a model never evaluated -- topic sentence and evidence are on different objects. 'Our insight: quantize first, evict last' -> maps. Contributions list -> maps. p2-p3 Related Work: 'Token eviction' / 'KV quantization' / 'Joint token-precision optimization' / 'Long-context KV inference' -> the first two map; the third has NO identifiable topic sentence -- it opens on MiniKV, becomes a MoE-nD positioning argument, becomes a results report, becomes a baselines caveat, becomes an xKV results report, and closes on KV Pareto. This paragraph maps to neither the thesis nor any single claim of its own and is the clearest deletion/split candidate in the paper. The 'Long-context KV inference' paragraph ends 'These approaches are orthogonal ... could in principle be combined' -- it maps to no claim the paper makes or tests, and is a deletion candidate. p3-p5 Method: 'Given a model with L layers and total memory budget B, we seek per-layer allocations' -> maps. 'Coverage models how much attention mass is captured' -> maps. 'Fidelity captures quantization quality loss' -> maps. 'Importance weights each layer's contribution to eviction sensitivity' -> topic sentence promises a principle; the paragraph's evidence establishes the OPPOSITE (the direction is architecture-dependent, flat on Qwen2.5-14B, inverted on Llama-2-13B) and then keeps the Mistral-tuned default anyway. Evidence does not map to its own topic sentence -- this is the paper's most important paragraph and it argues against itself. 'Weak correlation enables complementary allocation' -> the evidence (rho=0.194, n=22, not significant) does not support the topic sentence. 'The objective is an instance of MCKP' -> maps, and is the most disciplined paragraph in the paper. p5-p9 Experiments/Ablation/Analysis: setup, main results, long context, end-to-end, importance ablation, signal crossover, component analysis, mean-fill, downstream, why-quantization-alone-is-insufficient, allocator quality, Gini stability -> all map. 'Why quantization alone is insufficient' (p9) is the paper's true load-bearing argument and it appears on page 9, buried after MMLU/GSM8K/LongBench, in a paragraph with no table of its own; on a skim it is invisible. FINDING: two paragraphs map to neither thesis nor own evidence (the 32-line joint-optimization paragraph; the long-context-orthogonality paragraph), two have evidence contradicting their own topic sentence (Importance; Weak correlation), and the single paragraph that would justify the whole paper against its strongest baseline is misplaced on the last content page.

I inspected all three figures as rendered in the compiled PDF (all on p7) at 4-5x magnification. FIGURE 1 (ppl_scaling.pdf, two panels). Left: seven model curves, legend box overlapping the plot area at upper-left with ~4pt text; solid/dashed encodes GQA/MHA per the caption but four of the seven series are visually near-identical near y=1.0 and cannot be separated at print size; palette includes blue/orange/green/red/purple/brown/cyan (matplotlib default), which is not colorblind-safe for the red/green and orange/brown pairs. Right: DEFECT -- the StreamLLM (brown) curve is clipped by the y-limit at 1.35; its 4x and 6x points are off-scale and the line simply terminates at the frame with no break marker or note in the caption. SECOND DEFECT -- the caption states 'LayerBudget (bold) outperforms all eviction methods and matches KIVI at 2-3x', but the red LayerBudget curve at CR=6x sits at ~1.25, ABOVE H2O (green, ~1.158) and SnapKV (grey, ~1.245). The figure as drawn falsifies its own caption and Table 2's caption. Axis label 'Compression Ratio' with ticks at 2,3,4,6 on a linear axis makes the 4->6 segment visually twice as wide as 2->3, exaggerating the terminal slope of every curve. FIGURE 2 (allocation_heatmap.pdf, four panels). DEFECT -- the legend advertises three classes (FP16 green, INT8 orange, INT4 red) but FP16 appears in ZERO panels; an orphan legend entry that also contradicts Section 1's 'upgrades from INT4 to INT8/FP16 only at sensitive layers'. DEFECT -- the figure is on TinyLlama-1.1B (22 layers), a model absent from the seven-model suite and from every results table; the caption says so plainly ('on TinyLlama') without acknowledging the mismatch. DEFECT -- the 4x panel is uniformly INT4 across all layers, i.e. no per-layer precision at the paper's headline CR, which visually undercuts the 'Precision' half of the title. LEGIBILITY -- panel titles, both y-axis labels ('Token Fraction', 'Gini') and all tick labels render at roughly 3pt and are unreadable at print size; the dashed Gini overlay is a thin grey line barely distinguishable from the panel border. COLOR -- green/orange/red is the encoding channel and is the worst possible choice for deuteranopia. The 2x and 3x panels differ only in the orange/red boundary position and read as duplicates at a glance. FIGURE 3 (signal_curves.pdf, two panels). DEFECT -- the two panels use DIFFERENT colors for the SAME two series: left (TinyLlama-1.1B) uses blue for Gini and green for importance; right (Mistral-7B) uses orange for Gini and red for importance. Same figure, same quantities, incompatible encodings. DEFECT -- the rho annotation box at upper-left of each panel overlaps the axis frame and the first data point and is unreadable; the caption reports a single rho=0.194 without saying which of the two panels it belongs to. DEFECT -- pink and blue shaded bands (legend text unreadable, apparently 'Protected band' and 'Compress-first band') are never defined in the caption or anywhere in the text. Both legends sit on top of the descending data curves. Neither panel is identified by model in the caption. OVERALL: none of the three figures stands on its own, one contradicts its caption, one contains an element that contradicts the method description, and two are drawn on a model the paper does not evaluate. Nothing looks AI-generated in the diagrammatic sense (these are matplotlib outputs, not synthesized images), but they look unreviewed after compilation, which costs the same credibility.

(a) ANONYMITY: no violation found. The title block (p1) shows the standard 'Anonymous Author(s) / Affiliation / Address / email' placeholder; the footer reads 'Submitted to 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Do not distribute.' Concurrent work is referred to in third person ('Sun et al. 2026', 'Chang et al. 2025'); no self-identifying citation, acknowledgment, institution or repository URL appears. The checklist's 'An anonymized code repository is provided as supplementary material' (item 5) is correctly phrased. No aggressive priority claim beyond 'To our knowledge, no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l, b_l)' (p3), which is a standard novelty statement -- though it is factually endangered by RDKV and HqeKV (see P1). (b) COMPLETENESS: the NeurIPS Paper Checklist IS present, beginning on p13 and running to p18 with all 16 items answered, including item 16 (Declaration of LLM usage: N/A, with justification). PROBLEM: the checklist is interleaved with appendix Tables 8-21 because of float placement, so it does not read as a contiguous document -- items 7-8 are split across Tables 12/13 on p16 and items 15-16 across Tables 16/17 on p18. Not a desk-reject, but sloppy. MORE SERIOUS: item 3 ('Theory assumptions and proofs: Yes') justifies itself by citing 'the (1-1/e) approximation guarantee with a citation to Svirdenko 2004', a guarantee Section 3.5 explicitly disclaims. A checklist that certifies a theoretical guarantee the body denies is a completeness defect that an AC will notice. Items 1, 2, 4 and 13 also cite stale counts (five contributions vs six, four limitations vs five, <=3500 tokens vs 32K, 12 baselines vs 17). (c) FORMAT: main text ends on p9 (Conclusion closes at the foot of p9), references pp10-11, appendix and checklist pp11-19 -- compliant with 'nine content pages'. Template and margins appear unmodified. HOWEVER: Table 2 (p6) is wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}, which scales the table body to roughly 4pt -- well below the NeurIPS body font and below any reasonable legibility threshold; its footnote line is unreadable at 100%. The handbook states submissions 'violating the NeurIPS style (e.g., by decreasing margins or font sizes) ... may be desk rejected'. Shrinking the paper's principal results table below legibility is a genuine format risk and must be fixed by splitting the table, not by scaling it further.

(a) WHAT THE ALGORITHM ACTUALLY COMPUTES. Algorithm 1 (p11) initializes n_l = n_min, b_l = 4 for all l, then repeatedly applies the (layer, action) maximizing dQ/dM where Q = C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l, C = (n_l/S)^(1-g_l), F is a per-model cosine-similarity constant in {1.000, ~0.9998, ~0.976}, and w_l = sigmoid(5*(1 - l/(L-1) - 0.3)). So the solver maximizes a product of (i) a power-law surrogate for attention mass, (ii) a KV-tensor cosine similarity, and (iii) a hand-set depth prior. (b) DOES IT EQUAL THE OBJECT THE THEORY NAMES? Partly. The MCKP framing is honestly stated and the paper correctly declines the (1-1/e) bound. But Q is called a 'quality model' and is nowhere validated against quality. Only the C factor is calibrated, and only against attention mass on one model (MAE 3.1%, Mistral-7B). F is a cosine similarity between quantized and full KV tensors -- a tensor-reconstruction proxy, not a quality measure -- and the paper's own numbers show why that matters: F(4)=0.976 vs F(8)=0.9998 is a 2.2% gap in cosine, yet Table 3 shows the same allocator producing PPL ratios from 1.002 to 45.09 depending only on w. The multiplicative form Q = C*F*w is asserted, never derived or validated; there is no experiment showing that maximizing Q correlates with minimizing PPL. The one experiment that isolates the solver ('118-119% of the best 500-trial random-search quality score') measures Q itself, so it is circular -- it shows greedy maximizes Q better than random search, not that maximizing Q is the right thing to do. (c) SEMANTICS SILENTLY CHANGED. THE 'ONLINE' CLAIM. Table 4 (p12) differentiates LayerBudget from MoE-nD on exactly one axis: 'Online' vs 'offline'. But F(8) and F(4) are per-model constants measured offline over 8 WikiText-2 calibration prompts (Appendix D); the recommended deployment recipe is 'fixed profiles (calibrated once per model)' (Table 16 caption) plus 'a per-architecture importance direction (one bit per model, set from a 5-prompt LOO probe)' (Section 3.2). Every ingredient of the allocation -- fidelity constants, importance direction, and in deployment the Gini profile itself -- is offline-calibrated. The sole claimed differentiator against the closest concurrent work does not survive the paper's own recommended configuration. THE MEMORY MODEL. M(n,b) = 2nHd*b/8 presumes a packed mixed-bit cache. Table 13 measures 24.3% saving at nominal 2x on Llama-2-7B and Table 14 shows +2.6% to +12.2% TPOT overhead with Table 13's speedup below 1x in all nine rows, which is what one expects if layers are dequantized to FP16 before attention rather than served from a fused mixed-bit kernel. The paper never states which. If the cache is materialized in FP16 for attention, M(n,b) is not the object being optimized. THE IMPORTANCE PRIOR. w_l is presented as encoding 'eviction sensitivity', and Section 3.2 then reports LOO evidence that the sensitivity direction is late-biased on Llama-2-13B and flat on Qwen2.5-14B -- yet the early-biased default is used for all end-to-end results 'for consistency'. So for at least two of seven models the term the theory names (eviction sensitivity) is anti-correlated with the term the implementation uses. That is a theory/implementation mismatch, disclosed but not fixed.

CONTRIBUTIONS AS CLAIMED, IN ORDER (Section 1, p2). C1 per-layer (n_l,b_l) formalization + 'quantize-first' greedy solver with calibrated fidelity constants. C2 LOO discovery that early layers are the bottleneck + inverted importance. C3 mean-fill. C4 controlled comparison of 17 baselines, ranks 1st among token-reducing methods. C5 16K-32K validation. C6 72B scaling. ISOLATING EXPERIMENTS AND MEASURED MARGINAL EFFECT. C1: the ONLY isolating experiment is 'greedy achieves 118-119% of the best 500-trial random search' (Section 3.5, Section 6) -- measured on the surrogate Q, not on PPL, on one model, with no seeds or CI. There is NO experiment measuring the solver's PPL benefit over random search or over a fixed pyramid schedule. The closest proxy the paper does provide, Table 10's A3 row, removes the INT8 level entirely ({4,16} vs {4,8,16}) and the PPL ratios are BIT-IDENTICAL: Mistral 1.01/1.00 at 3x and 3.23/3.23 at 6x; Llama-2 1.02/1.02 and 45.09/45.09. So the mixed-precision degree of freedom -- the 'Precision' in the title -- has a measured marginal effect of at most 0.01 and usually exactly zero. C2: isolated in Table 3. Marginal effect is enormous: replacing inverted with sigmoid moves Llama-2-7B at 6x from 1.002 to 45.09 (45x) and Mistral from 1.283 to 3.231 (2.5x). C3: isolated by comparing Table 3/Table 8 (zero-fill) against Section 6 (mean-fill). Marginal effect is enormous: Llama-2-7B at 6x, 45.09 -> 1.13; logits KL 0.6696 -> 0.0636. The paper also reports that median-fill and random-fill work equally well, so the effect belongs to 'fill with something distributionally sane', not to mean-fill specifically. C4: not a method contribution; the ranking claim is false at Mistral 6x (see P5). C5 and C6 are coverage, isolated by construction. RANKING BY MEASURED EFFECT: mean-fill (~40x) > importance direction (~45x, and it is a single sign bit set by hand) >> greedy joint allocation (1.19x on a surrogate, 0x from the INT8 level). RANKING IMPLIED BY THE ABSTRACT AND TITLE: joint (n_l,b_l) allocation first (it is the title), importance second, mean-fill third. THE ORDERING IS INVERTED. The paper is named after, and led by, the component with the weakest isolating evidence -- and that evidence is measured on the method's own surrogate objective rather than on any reported metric. The two components carrying the results are a hand-set sigmoid sign and a one-line imputation rule that the paper itself says can be replaced by median or random fill. This is the P12 fatal pattern: a contribution billed as primary whose isolating experiment shows a small or unmeasured effect. The honest fix is to retitle around mean-fill + layer-direction-aware eviction and demote the joint solver, not to argue for the solver.

(a) ONE-SENTENCE CONTRIBUTION IN THIS COMMUNITY'S VOCABULARY: 'A training-free KV-cache compression method that allocates a per-layer token budget and quantization bit-width jointly under a global memory budget using a greedy marginal-gain heuristic, achieving near-lossless perplexity at 2-4x compression on 7B-72B models.' That sentence composes cleanly from standard efficient-inference vocabulary, so the venue-fit test is passed at the topical level -- this is a NeurIPS/ICLR/MLSys paper, not a mis-venued one. (b) TERMS A PC MEMBER WOULD HAVE TO LOOK UP -- none are foreign to the field, but four are the authors' coinages used as if established: 'coverage law' (their power-law surrogate), 'mean-fill' (imputation of evicted KV), 'inverted importance' (early-biased depth prior), 'LayerBudget-KV' / 'LB-KV'. Also 'Ph'/'Qt'/'Jt' in Table 2, never expanded. (c) NO MECHANISM BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT COMMUNITY. The MCKP framing is textbook OR but is used only descriptively. I would not forward this elsewhere on topical grounds. (d) THE REAL FIT PROBLEM IS THE BAR AND THE BENCHMARK SET, NOT THE ROOM. The paper positions against 2024-2025 literature (H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, KIVI, StreamingLLM) and two 2026 preprints it re-implements, while the venue's current bar in this exact niche is 14-40x compression (MoE-nD 14x; STAR-KV, ICML 2026 Spotlight, 20x; KVTC, ICLR 2026, 20-40x; ThinKV at <5% cache; RDKV at 2.48% retention). LayerBudget's usable envelope is 2-4x and it degrades sharply at 6x. Its primary metric is WikiText-2 perplexity, which this community has largely retired as a compression metric; the benchmark set the field now expects (LongBench-v2, RULER 4K-128K, InfiniteBench, SCBench, HELMET, and AIME/MATH-500/GPQA/LiveCodeBench for reasoning models) is represented only by LongBench-v1 (at a broken scale) and RULER at 4K on one model. The evaluation-methodology literature the community now expects papers to respect -- matched-budget query-visibility audits, backend-sensitivity controls, KVPress as the common harness -- is not engaged. So: correct room, but the paper reads as arriving one generation late in both operating point and evaluation protocol. That is a Contribution/Significance problem rather than a mis-venuing one, and I am scoring it as such.

(a) EXPECTED METRICS FOR KV-CACHE COMPRESSION IN 2026. Perplexity: REPORTED (primary). NIAH: REPORTED (4K only, 10 depths x 3 needles = 30 trials per cell, no CI). RULER: REPORTED but only at 4K and only on Qwen2.5-72B (Table 21); the 4K-128K sweep the field expects is OMITTED. LongBench-v1: REPORTED but at an evidently broken scale (0.040-0.056 for every method including Full KV). LongBench-v2: OMITTED. InfiniteBench: OMITTED. SCBench: OMITTED. HELMET: OMITTED. Reasoning suite (AIME 24/25, MATH-500, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench): OMITTED entirely -- and this is the regime where hybrid quantization+eviction is currently most contested (ThinKV, MixKVQ). MMLU: REPORTED. GSM8K: REPORTED (200 samples, at floor on Llama-2-7B). Effective bits per token, the field's common currency alongside CR: OMITTED. Decode throughput / TTFT: partially -- TPOT is reported (Table 14) and is negative (+2.6% to +12.2%), end-to-end speedup (Table 13) is below 1x in all nine rows. Peak memory at the long-context operating point: OMITTED -- memory is measured only at 512/1024/4096 tokens, never at the 16K/32K where the paper argues compression matters most. (b) DOES A HEADLINE CLAIM DEPEND ON AN OMITTED METRIC? Yes, two. First, effective bits/token and per-cell measured bytes: the entire 'ranks 1st' claim is stated at nominal CR, and Table 13 shows nominal CR does not correspond to a fixed measured reduction (1.32x-3.50x at nominal 2x). Reporting bits/token would have caught this. Second, long-context peak memory: the abstract's and conclusion's motivation is memory at long context, and the 32K experiments report only PPL. If the mixed-bit cache is dequantized to FP16 for attention (which the sub-1x speedups suggest), the 32K memory benefit may not exist at all -- an omitted metric that could reverse the paper's central motivating claim. (c) UNMEASURED TERMS IN THE PAPER'S OWN OBJECTIVE. Q = C * F * w. The C factor is validated against attention mass (MAE 3.1%, one model). The F factor is a cosine similarity, never related to any quality outcome. The w factor is a hand-set sigmoid that is never measured against anything -- and the paper's own LOO probe shows its direction is wrong for Llama-2-13B and irrelevant for Qwen2.5-14B, yet it is used everywhere. So two of the three multiplicands in the optimized objective are never validated against the metric the paper reports, and there is no experiment showing that higher Q implies lower PPL. That is an unmeasured term in the objective, which is a defect independent of field convention. (d) WORKLOAD REGIME VS CLAIMS. The claims are stated over 'seven models from 7B to 72B' and 'long context', but: 72B is evaluated only at 1024 tokens PPL plus 4K NIAH/RULER; 32K is evaluated only on two models (Qwen3-8B OOMed) and only on PPL; end-to-end vLLM integration is validated at 512 tokens; MMLU/GSM8K/LongBench are all at <=4096. The regime where the method is claimed to matter most (long context, large model, downstream task) is the one regime never jointly evaluated.
